battle.name: 神川之戰
battle.brief: 延暦13年（794）七月，隼人與大隅人舉兵，朝廷遣藤原魚名、大伴弟麻呂率軍南下，於大隅國神川之濱一戰而潰其眾，大隅全境平定。卡面希臘重步兵並無涉此役，但圓盾結陣、互相遮蔽的思路，與官軍以大楯列陣、弓兵在後壓制的打法可對照：一個靠常備公民兵與正面強度，一個靠兵種分工與地形切割。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries: 延暦13年（794）神川之戰的交戰雙方，是日本律令國家的朝廷軍與南九州隼人・大隅人的聯軍。朝廷一方名義上出自桓武天皇的敕命，實際由攝政院與式部省調度，兵員來自律令國家的三套制度：國府與國分寺的鎮兵、由良田墾成的兵團屯田，以及自都城直接派出的蕃兵與雜兵。歷次征隼人，都由藤原與大伴兩家派出大將，掛「征隼人使」或「征薩珈帥」的名號領兵，大權握在兩家將門手中。隼人一方不是國家，而是大隅國熊野郡、姶良郡、垂水郡，薩摩國甑原郡與豐後國速見郡的氏族聯盟，以「隼人長」為首領，以村落、山林與海岸地帶為根據地。大隅人並非隼人，但有自己的首長與土地，在朝廷的國造制度下正被逐步編入律令籍，這場戰爭實為隼人反抗朝廷直接編管大隅的一次總爆發。雙方的指揮系統簡陋而懸殊：朝廷有詔令、有國府、有固定的糧秣輸送線，人數卻受制於國庫；隼人沒有常設軍令，首領靠血緣與地域紐帶臨時聚合，一旦糧道被切或首長陣亡即告瓦解。隼人沒有固定的常備軍，也沒有攻城器械，這正是律令方以封鎖、撫慰與編制代替正面消耗的依據。
countriesEn: The two sides in the Battle of Kamikawa of 794 (Enryaku 13) were the court army of the Japanese ritsuryo state on one hand and, on the other, a coalition of Hayato and Osumi people from southern Kyushu. The court side acted in the name of an order of Emperor Kanmu but was in fact directed by the regency office and the Ministry of Ceremonies, and drew its soldiers from three institutions of the ritsuryo state: the garrison troops of the provincial governments and the provincial temples, the heitai, that is the soldier-farmers of the tonden, and troops and miscellaneous levies sent straight out of the capital. For every campaign against the Hayato a great commander drawn from one of the two great houses, the Fujiwara or the Otomo, was appointed with the title of Se Hayato-shi or Se Satsuka-kanbei, and real command lay in the hands of those two houses. The Hayato side was not a state but a league of lineages from the Kumano, Aira and Tarumi districts of Osumi province, from Koshima district of Satsuma, and from Hayami district of Bungo, led by chiefs called Hayato-nagomi and holding the villages, the forested hills and the coastal strips as their bases. The Osumi people were not Hayato, but they had their own chiefs and their own land, and under the kokushi system of the court they were being drawn step by step into the ritsuryo registers; this war was in truth the great eruption of a Hayato resistance to the direct administration of Osumi. The two command systems were both crude and wildly unequal. The court had decrees, provincial administrations and fixed lines of supply, but its numbers were constrained by the treasury. The Hayato had no standing command, and their leaders drew together through kinship and local ties; once the supply line was cut or a chief fell, the force dissolved. The Hayato had no regular army and no siege engines, and that is precisely why the ritsuryo side answered with blockade, pacification and registration in place of a frontal grinding contest.
people: 這場戰爭牽涉的人物可以分三層。第一層是打了一場持久戰的藤原仲麻呂（726–784）：天應元年（779）朝廷任命他為征薩珈帥，他在大隅苦戰一年，天應二年（780）平定大隅，隼人首領以「虎印」相贈，這枚印後來在朝議中反覆成為是非之源；延暦三年（784），他在大伴氏宅中被毒身亡，藤原氏把持朝政的長期格局由此奠定。第二層是完成最後一役的將領：延暦13年（794）受命出征的是藤原魚名與大伴弟麻呂，魚名時任薩摩守並被授征隼人使，弟麻呂則是大伴紀麻呂之侄、光明皇之弟，兩人分領兵眾南北夾擊，魚名事後累升至攝政，弟麻呂亦以軍功晉爵。第三層是前輩與善後的執行者：大伴紀麻呂早在天平寶字年間（762–763）就以征隼人使的身份平定豐後隼人，是大伴氏在隼人問題上的既有功業；仲麻呂之弟藤原宇通在仲麻呂死後接任攝政，主持隼人善後與大隅設郡的準備；隼人那邊留下的是首長的官銜，「隼人長」「國造」這類頭銜記錄了他們如何被朝廷用名位收編。至於具體的隼人首領姓名，現存史籍多以郡鄉與部族概稱，個別首領的記載散佚，難以一一列名，戰史所存者多是「某郡隼人」一類的集體稱呼。
peopleEn: The people involved in this war fall into three layers. The first is Fujiwara no Nakamaro (726-784), who fought the long war: in 780 (Tenno 1, 779) the court appointed him Se Satsuka-kanbei, and after a hard year in Osumi he put down the province in Tenno 2 (780), and the Hayato chiefs presented him a tiger tally in token of submission, a token that later became a repeated source of dispute in court debate. In Enryaku 3 (784) he was poisoned in a residence of the Otomo house, and the long pattern of Fujiwara dominance at court dates from there. The second layer is the commanders who fought the last action: those dispatched in Enryaku 13 (794) were Fujiwara no Uona and Otomo no Otomaro, with Uona serving as governor of Satsuma and appointed Se Hayato-shi, and Otomaro, a nephew of Otomo no Kimaro and brother of the emperor Konin, taking charge of part of the force, the two working from separate lines so as to close in from north and south; Uona was later raised step by step to the regency, and Otomaro was ennobled for his services. The third layer is the predecessors and the men who carried out the settlement: Otomo no Kimaro had already been appointed Se Hayato-shi and had put down the Hayato of Bungo back in the Tenpyo Hōji years (762-763), which was the standing credit of the Otomo house in this business; Fujiwara no Utono, brother of Nakamaro, took over the regency after Nakamaro's death and presided over the settlement of the Hayato and the preparations for making Osumi a province; and on the Hayato side what survives are the official titles of the chiefs, the Hayato-nagomi and the kokushi, recording how they were taken over by the court through rank and title. As for the personal names of the Hayato leaders themselves, the surviving histories mostly refer to them collectively by district and tribe, and the record of individual chiefs is fragmentary, so they cannot be listed one by one; what the chronicles preserve is such collective forms as the Hayato of a certain district.
kits: 卡面這名希臘重步兵（hoplite）從未踏上日本的土地，他是公元前五世紀的希臘城邦重裝步兵：左手圓盾（aspis，木胎蒙皮再包青銅，直徑約九十至一百公分），右手短劍（xiphos，直刃約六十公分，必要時反手刺出），身前握一支矛（dory，長約二點四至二點七公尺），頭戴科林斯式或雅典式青銅盔，著亞麻或青銅胸甲與脛甲，全副裝備約七百至九百克。整套裝備的邏輯是遮蔽而非格鬥：圓盾並排即成一面牆，前排的體格支撐住後排的進退，個人武藝被陣形吸收。而794年神川之戰的裝備完全是另一套系統。朝廷軍以大楯（圓形或橢圓形的大盾）列於前，弓兵以和弓與鐵鏃在後射擊，鎧以革甲為主、發給將士的是鐵鎧，配直刀與短刀，攜帶三日分糧與竹筒，另有騎兵與傳令；隼人一方用短弓、直刃手刀、木盾與皮甲，尤以騎射見長，人數不多但能在海岸山地之間流動襲擾。攻城方面雙方都沒有大型器械，隼人只在石山城以土壘木柵倚山為固，官軍的辦法是封鎖、斷糧、誘降。運輸靠船與馬，官軍從筑前、豐前走海路運兵運糧，隼人則以游擊切割這條糧線，這是雙方勝負的真正著力點。
kitsEn: The Greek hoplite on the card never set foot in Japan. He was a heavy infantryman of the Greek city states of the fifth century BC: a round shield on the left arm, the aspis, wooden core covered with hide and faced with bronze, about ninety to one hundred centimetres across; a short sword in the right hand, the xiphos, a straight blade of about sixty centimetres, used in a reverse grip when the shield had to stay in place; a spear in front of him, the dory, about two point four to two point seven metres long; a Corinthian or Attic bronze helmet; a linen or bronze cuirass and greaves; the whole load weighing roughly seven hundred to nine hundred grams. The logic of the whole kit is cover rather than duel: when the round shields are set side by side they become a wall, the physique of the front rank bears the advance and withdrawal of the ranks behind, and the individual skill of the fighter is absorbed into the formation. The equipment at the Battle of Kamikawa in 794 was a completely different system. The court army set the dai Tate, the large round or oval shield, in front, with archers behind firing the yumi and iron-tipped arrows; armour was leather for the rank and file and iron for the commanders, with straight and short swords; three days of rations and bamboo tubes for water were carried, and there were cavalry and messengers as well. The Hayato used short bows, single-edged hand swords, wooden shields and leather armour, and were best noted for riding and shooting, few in number but able to move and strike between coast and mountain. Neither side had heavy siege machinery: the Hayato did no more at the Castle of Ishiyama than raise earthen works and wooden fences against the hill, and the court's answer was blockade, cutting of supplies and induced surrender. Movement and supply relied on ships and horses; the court carried troops and grain by sea from Chikuzen and Bungo, and the Hayato cut that line with raids, which was the real point on which the contest turned.
tactics: 隼人這一方打的是不對稱的消耗戰。他們不與官軍在開闊地會戰，而是退入南九州的山林與海岸地帶，以村落為基點，游擊糧道、襲擊屯田、焚燒糧秣，逼官軍分散駐軍；石山城這類依山臨海的砦點，則在需要決戰時用來固守。朝廷的戰術框架有三層：分兵，以國府鎮兵在要點屯守，以兵團屯田維持糧源，以海路分遣別將繞擊叛軍後方，切斷其與首領的聯繫；編制，把已降的隼人整編為先鋒與嚮導，用熟悉山路的當地人引導官軍逐點攻破據點；以及最關鍵的政治戰，以「隼人長」「國造」的頭銜換取服從，以授田、編戶與賞賜把叛軍首領拉進律令體系，並用禁絕水市交易的辦法斷掉隼人賴以生存的走私收入。794年7月的神川之戰，官軍在灣岸狹窄處以弓兵壓制、盾兵接戰、騎兵策應，一戰而潰敵，這種打法與希臘方陣的正面硬撼恰好相反：希臘人靠圓盾互相遮蔽換取正面不敗，日本官軍靠兵種分工與地形切割換取對手崩散。制度差異比裝備差異更關鍵，希臘方陣的全盛期已過三百多年，8世紀日本的律令軍則早已不是常備公民兵，而是半農半兵的屯田兵，戰力隨財政枯竭而下滑。
tacticsEn: The Hayato fought an asymmetric war of attrition. They did not meet the court army in the open, but drew back into the hills and coastal belt of southern Kyushu, made villages their bases, raided supply lines, struck at the tonden fields and burned grain stores, and forced the government to scatter its garrisons. Fortified points such as the Castle of Ishiyama, built on a hill above the sea, were held for the moment when a decisive action was unavoidable. The court's tactical frame had three layers. First, dispersion: garrison troops of the provincial governments held the key points, the tonden heitai kept the grain coming, and detachments sent by sea swung round behind the rebels to cut them off from their chiefs. Second, conversion: Hayato who had already submitted were enrolled as skirmishers and guides, and local men who knew the mountain paths led the court army point by point against the strongholds. Third, and the most important of all, political warfare: the titles of Hayato-nagomi and kokushi were handed out in exchange for obedience, land grants, registration and rewards were used to draw rebel chiefs into the ritsuryo order, and trade with the Hayato through the water markets was forbidden so as to cut the smuggling income on which they lived. At the battle of Kamikawa in July 794 the court army worked along the narrow shore of the bay, with archers pressing, shielded infantry closing, and cavalry covering the flanks, and the enemy collapsed in a single action. The method is the exact opposite of the frontal grinding of the Greek phalanx: the Greeks won an unbreakable front through shields that covered one another, while the Japanese court army won through the division of arms and through cutting the ground into pieces. The difference in institution mattered more than the difference in equipment, for the heyday of the Greek phalanx was already more than three centuries past, and the ritsuryo army of the eighth century was no longer a force of full-time citizens at all but of half-farming, half-fighting tonden soldiers whose strength declined as the finances ran dry.
data: 可核對的數字分三類。第一類是系年：隼人之亂起於寶龜元年（770），天應二年（780）藤原仲麻呂平定大隅，延暦13年（794）七月神川合戰，同年大隅全境平定，至延暦18年（799）朝廷正式設置大隅國，前後延續約二十四年。神川之戰的日期一般記為延暦13年七月廿八日，按日本曆換算約在公曆同年8月下旬。第二類是地理與行政：神川一般認為即今大隅縣的高隅川，石山城一般認為即今南九州市皴ヶ崎一帶的海岬，戰地在大隅國熊野郡，與薩摩國分界；自薩摩一帶的入海口沿海南下至戰場，現代公路里程約六十公里。隼人分布的郡可以列舉：大隅國熊野郡、姶良郡、垂水郡，薩摩國甑原郡，豐後國速見郡。第三類是必須打折扣的推估：兩軍實際出戰人數史無明文，只能從律令兵制推想，兵團屯田以八年為一輪，兵農合一，每次遠征真正可動員的兵力有限，多在數千量級；隼人一方歷次聚兵的人數亦無確數。另有考古與碑刻可作旁證：大隅國府一帶的官廳遺跡，以及後世留下的《敦賀隼人碑》，記錄隼人被編入越前國敦賀郡之事，該碑年代至今仍有異說，引用時須存疑。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The first is chronology: the Hayato rising began in 770 (Hoki 1); Nakamaro put down Osumi in 780 (Tenno 2); the battle of Kamikawa was fought in the seventh month of 794 (Enryaku 13), and Osumi was pacified in the same year; the province of Osumi was formally established in 799 (Enryaku 18), so the affair ran for about twenty-four years from end to end. The date of the battle is generally given as the twenty-eighth day of the seventh month of Enryaku 13, which in the Japanese calendar falls in the latter part of August of the same year in the Gregorian reckoning. The second class is geography and administration: the Kamikawa is generally identified with the Takasumi River in present-day Kagoshima Prefecture, and the Castle of Ishiyama generally with the cape at Kasugazaki in the city of Minamikyushu today, the battlefield lying in Kumano district of Osumi province on the border with Satsuma; from the landing places in Satsuma the army moved south along the coast, a run of some sixty kilometres by modern road. The districts in which the Hayato were settled can be listed: Kumano, Aira and Tarumi in Osumi province, Koshima in Satsuma, and Hayami in Bungo. The third class is estimate and must be discounted. Neither side has any figure in the record for the numbers actually engaged, and one can only reason from the ritsuryo military system: the heitai of the tonden served on an eight-year cycle, the same men were farmers and soldiers, and the force that could really be moved on a distant expedition was limited, on the order of several thousand; the numbers the Hayato mustered on their successive risings are equally unknown. Archaeology and inscriptions provide collateral evidence: the ruins of the provincial office in the Osumi capital area, and the Kayabaru Hayato stele left by later generations, which records the Hayato being enrolled in Hayano district of Echizen province, though the date of that stele remains disputed and must be treated with caution.
cause: 打起來有四層原因疊在一起。第一層是土地與稅役：律令國家要在南九州設郡置吏、徵調丁口、築城開墾，而隼人的生產方式長期倚賴山林與海岸的採集、漁獵與小塊耕作，一旦被編入調庸與兵役，負擔驟增。地理是底層原因：大隅的山地與海岸線極長，國府與國分寺的鎮兵只佔少數據點，控制線隨之外推到隼人聚落之間，摩擦不可避免。第二層是律令財政的崩壞：743年行三世一身法，其後庸調法逐步施行，丁口銳減而國府收入不穩，兵團屯田被大量抽調遠征，南九州的兵源與糧源同時吃緊，朝廷對隼人的每一次用兵都更急、更粗。第三層是朝堂的權力鬥爭：寶龜之亂（764）之後藤原仲麻呂集權，每一次征隼人都是替自己攢政治資本的機會，大伴氏系也靠戰功維持門第，兩家都需要一場可以向朝廷宣示的勝利。第四層是794年的直接導火線：朝廷在薩摩與大隅重新徵集隼人充兵、徵稅、修建城柵，並以新的郡縣編制逐步取代隼人長的傳統權力，隼人拒絕被這樣編管，遂再度舉兵。
causeEn: Four layers of cause lie piled one on another. The first is land and taxation. The ritsuryo state wished to establish districts and officials in southern Kyushu, to levy corvee labour, to build fortifications and to open ground to cultivation, while the economy of the Hayato had long rested on gathering, fishing and small-scale cultivation in the hills and along the coast; once they were entered into the registers of tax and service the burden jumped at once. Geography is the cause underneath everything: the mountains and the coastline of Osumi are enormously long, the garrisons of the provincial governments and the provincial temples occupy only a few points, and the line of control is pushed out in between the Hayato villages, so friction was unavoidable. The second layer is the collapse of ritsuryo finances: the three-generation one-register rule of 743 and the gradual introduction of the yōchō law after it reduced the number of registered households while the provincial revenues stayed unstable, and the tonden heitai were repeatedly stripped out for distant campaigns, so the man-power and the grain of southern Kyushu were strained at the same time, and every expedition against the Hayato was undertaken with more haste and less care. The third layer is the struggle for power at court. After the Hōki no ran of 764 Nakamaro had concentrated authority, and every campaign against the Hayato was an opportunity to pile up political capital for himself, while the Otomo line needed victories to keep its standing; both houses wanted a success they could display. The fourth layer is the immediate spark of 794: the court once more levied Hayato as soldiers in Satsuma and Osumi, levied taxes and built fences, and began to replace the traditional authority of the Hayato chiefs with the new district administration of the ritsuryo state; the Hayato refused to be administered in this way, and rose once more.
impact: 神川之戰是隼人之亂的最後一場大規模戰鬥，它的結果是律令國家在南九州的直接統治落地。戰後隼人由武裝的部族逐步變成律令籍的編戶，大隅國於799年設置，隼人首長以「隼人長」「國造」的頭銜被任用作郡級的唐朝官，隼人居民開始負擔調庸與兵役；一批隼人又被移配到內地的州郡，試圖以分散居住切斷其故鄉的組織能力，這是日本國家第一次系統地以編戶化的辦法處理南方異族問題。日後隼人並未消失：他們在十二世紀以隼人商人與水市特權的身份重新出現在南國的貿易網絡中，成為中世南九州商業的活線。戰爭的代價同樣明顯，二十餘年的反覆出征耗盡國府財力，九州的兵團與鎮兵凋零，十一世紀初國司府已名存實亡，財政轉而向藤原家的私請依存；朝廷對隼人的記錄也從戰報逐漸凝固為定型化的異族形象，寫在《續日本紀》與後來的地方風土記裡，成了下一千年日本知識中一個固定的名詞。
impactEn: The Battle of Kamikawa was the last large-scale action of the Hayato rising, and its result was the landing of direct ritsuryo rule in southern Kyushu. After it the Hayato passed gradually from armed clansmen to registered households in the ritsuryo registers: the province of Osumi was established in 799, Hayato chiefs were appointed in the titles of Hayato-nagomi and kokushi to serve as Tang-style officials of district rank, and the Hayato population began to bear tax and service; a further body of Hayato was relocated to the provinces of the interior, an attempt to break up the organisation of their home country by scattering them, and the first systematic effort by the Japanese state to handle a southern people by registering them. The Hayato did not afterwards disappear: in the twelfth century they reappeared in the trade network of the southern provinces as Hayato merchants enjoying the privileges of the water markets, and became a living strand of the commerce of southern Kyushu in the medieval period. The cost of the war is just as clear: twenty-odd years of repeated expeditions drained the provincial treasuries, the heitai and the garrisons of Kyushu fell away, and by the early eleventh century the provincial governments were nominal, with the finances coming to depend on the private levies of the Fujiwara. The court's own record of the Hayato also hardened from a series of campaign reports into a fixed image of an alien people, written down in the Shoku Nihon-ki and later in the local gazetteers, and it became for the next thousand years a settled noun in Japanese knowledge.
result: 延暦13年（794）七月廿八日，朝廷軍在神川之濱擊破隼人・大隅的聯軍，叛軍潰散，首領降伏，大隅全境隨之平定。善後工作延續了數年：799年大隅國設置，隼人長受任為郡級的唐朝官，隼人居民編入調庸與兵役，另有隼人被移配到越前、越中等內地郡縣，以分散居住削弱其故鄉的組織；隼人在新體制之下仍保有隼人水市與隼人質屋這一類交易的特權，成為中世南國商業的種子。代價寫在帳上：二十四年的戰爭把九州國府的兵源與財源壓到極限，鎮兵與屯田凋敝，國司府在十一世紀初形同虛設。戰役本身的細節因《延暦年紀》等史籍散佚而無從復原，能確定的只有大略：最後一役在神川一次會戰即告結束，此後南九州再無大規模的武裝抗爭。回頭看卡面那名希臘重步兵：他的方陣代表的是以常備公民兵支撐正面、以裝備與體格換取勝率的典範，而794年真正困住日本朝廷的並不是戰技，是律令國家的兵源與財政。希臘人的方陣在幾百年內被長槍與騎兵改寫，日本律令軍的末路則是把重裝步兵的份量，交給了後來的弓騎與水軍。
resultEn: On the twenty-eighth day of the seventh month of Enryaku 13 (794), the court army broke the Hayato-Osumi coalition on the bank of the Kamikawa; the rebels dissolved, their chiefs submitted, and all of Osumi was pacified in the same stroke. The settlement ran on for several years afterwards: the province of Osumi was established in 799, Hayato chiefs were appointed as Tang-style officials of district rank, the Hayato population was entered into the registers for tax and service, and further groups of Hayato were relocated to interior districts such as Hayano and Etchu, so as to weaken the organisation of their own country by scattering them; and under the new order the Hayato still kept the trading privileges of the Hayato water markets and the Hayato pawnshops, which became the seed of the commercial life of the southern provinces in the medieval period. The cost is written in the account: twenty-four years of war pushed the man-power and the wealth of the Kyushu provincial governments to the limit, the garrisons and the tonden withered away, and by the early eleventh century the provincial governments existed in name only. The details of the action itself cannot be recovered, because such records as the Enryaku nenki are lost; what can be established is the outline: the last battle ended in a single meeting engagement at the Kamikawa, and after it there was no large-scale armed resistance in southern Kyushu again. Looking back at the Greek hoplite on the card: his phalanx stands for the classic model of a front sustained by full-time citizens and a victory rate bought with equipment and physique, whereas what really hemmed the Japanese court in in 794 was not the quality of fighting but the man-power and the finances of the ritsuryo state. The Greek phalanx was rewritten within a few centuries by the long pike and the cavalry; the end of the Japanese ritsuryo army handed the weight of the heavy infantryman over to the mounted archers and the fleets that came after.
